Custom Whisky Cylinder Tube Packaging: Specs and Sourcing Guide

Published August 21, 2026 · Buyer guide · By BestPackFactory

Quick answer

A paper tube for whisky is a spiral-wound or convolute paperboard cylinder, typically 1.5-3.0 mm wall, with a telescoping or plug lid, printed on the full circumference. Size the interior at bottle diameter plus 3-5 mm and bottle height plus 10-15 mm for the end cap and liner. MOQ starts at 1,000 pieces, samples in 10-14 days, bulk 25-35 days. Confirm the liner grips the bottle so it cannot slide during transit.

Tube construction basics

Spiral-wound tubes are made by wrapping paperboard strips at an angle, giving strong walls for tall bottles; convolute tubes wind layers vertically and suit short, wide formats. Specify wall thickness by bottle weight: 1.5-2.0 mm for bottles up to 1 kg, 2.5-3.0 mm for heavier or gifting sets. Ask for the end-cap style: plug lid, telescoping cap or a flat bottom with slip lid.

360-degree printing and finishes

The tube circumference prints as one continuous panel, so artwork should be delivered as a flat layout matching the exact developed width. Confirm resolution and the bleed allowance the factory needs (usually 3-5 mm at each end). Foil stamping and spot UV are possible on tubes but check registration on the seam line; keep fine text away from the seam. Matte lamination is common to protect the print during handling.

Bottle sizing and inner liner

Measure the bottle at its widest point and add 3-5 mm for the tube interior diameter; add 10-15 mm of height for the end cap plus a foam or pulp liner that cups the base. The liner must hold the bottle firmly: a bottle that slides in the tube is the top damage complaint. Request a packed drop test at 60-80 cm and a fit sample with the actual bottle before bulk.

MOQ, lead time and gifting logistics

Tube MOQ usually starts at 1,000 pieces; windowed or sleeved gift sets at 2,000. Samples take 10-14 days (tube printing setup is slower than flat boxes), and bulk runs 25-35 days. If the tube ships inside a carton, confirm the carton depth so end caps are not compressed; a 3-5% overage order covers QC and transit damage for holiday peaks.

Buyer checklist

  1. Specify tube construction (spiral vs convolute) and wall thickness by bottle weight
  2. Measure bottle at widest point, add 3-5 mm diameter and 10-15 mm height allowance
  3. Confirm liner grips the bottle and request a packed 60-80 cm drop test
  4. Deliver 360-degree artwork as a flat layout with the factory bleed spec
  5. Order 10-14 days for samples and 3-5% overage for peak-season runs

Frequently asked questions

What wall thickness does a whisky tube need?

1.5-2.0 mm spiral-wound paperboard handles bottles up to about 1 kg; go to 2.5-3.0 mm for heavier bottles or gift sets. Confirm with the factory based on your bottle weight.

How is artwork handled on a round tube?

The tube prints as one continuous 360-degree panel, so supply a flat layout at the exact developed width with the factory's bleed allowance, usually 3-5 mm per end. Keep fine text away from the seam.

Why do tube samples take longer?

Tube printing and winding need dedicated setup, so samples typically take 10-14 days versus 7-10 for flat boxes, and bulk production runs 25-35 days. Plan the timeline accordingly.

What the Spec Means for Buyers

Whisky cylinder tubes are a round-structure project. Rigid board 1200/1500/1800 gsm greyboard wrapped in 157 gsm C1S art paper or 120 gsm specialty paper forms the tube; end caps are confirmed for fit. Finishes include matte lamination, soft-touch, hot foil and embossing; a fabric pouch or paperboard tray can hold the bottle. Corner and fit tolerances follow the rigid-box standard (corner gap ≤ 1.5 mm). Each tube passes a 24 h static load test. MOQ is 500 PCS per size and artwork.

Frequently Asked Questions

What board builds a cylinder tube?

1200–1800 gsm greyboard wrapped in 157 gsm art paper or 120 gsm specialty paper, with confirmed end-cap fit.

What finish suits a whisky tube?

Matte or soft-touch lamination with hot foil logo and optional embossing.
